Project File 01 / Simulation Evidence

MHDA —
denoise the signal.

Monolithic Hybrid Denoising Accelerator · Fixed-point signal processing and a compact MLP in SystemVerilog.

SystemVerilog · Python · Q1.15 Datapath ● Patent disclosure package prepared
01 / The goal
02 / The design
03 / Evidence

The problem

Build a hardware pipeline for acoustic denoising that combines adaptive filtering with a learned nonlinear correction. The target use cases include underwater acoustics and voice endpoints.

The design

An 8-tap RLS stage feeds an 8→128→384→128→1 MLP. The datapath uses signed Q1.15 fixed-point arithmetic with 40-bit accumulation. The pipeline is designed to run at 100 MHz; implementation and validation evidence stay tied to the numerical contract.

Architecture: Reference input → 8-tap RLS filter → MLP residual correction → Denoised output.

What the current simulation report says

  • RLS contribution: 5.0818 dB reported improvement.
  • MLP contribution: 3.7095 dB reported improvement.
  • Total reported SNR improvement: 8.7913 dB.
  • Maximum hardware/software error in report: 2.62 LSB.

These are repository-backed simulation results, not silicon measurements. They depend on the stimuli and reference fixed-point model used in the report.

Open work

Preserve the numerical quirks in the frozen contract, reproduce the results from a clean checkout, and keep ASIC implementation claims separate from RTL simulation. The prepared patent material is a disclosure package; it is not a granted patent.
